nodes.long_description:
1. Watch and catch the ruler falling in a well-lit area.
2. Listen to the sound of the ruler falling in the dark and catch it.

<Result
1. when looking and catching: light stimulus → visual cell → visual nerve → cerebrum → spinal cord → motor nerve → hand muscle → reaction (catching the ruler)
2 When listening and grasping: sound stimulus → auditory cells → auditory nerve → cerebrum → spinal cord → motor nerve → hand muscles → response (grasping the ruler)

 Understand that this is due to the different pathways the stimulus travels and the different speeds at which the brain processes information about the stimulus
nodes.short_description: Experiment with the difference in reaction time between catching a falling ballpoint pen in virtual reality using sight and hearing.

nodes.long_description: "Dive into the realm of realistic experiments through Virtual Reality (VR). Experience the excitement of conducting actual reactions in a risk-free digital laboratory. Mix substances, observe genuine changes, and engage with lifelike molecular structures—all in an immersive 3D environment. Enhance your learning by interacting with accurate representations of laboratory equipment and substances, all while honing your scientific skills. Explore the world of chemistry in an unprecedented way, where hands-on experimentation meets cutting-edge technology for an educational adventure like no other.
